questions.question: Describe the Jenkins continuous-integration setup you worked with at Pitney Bowes. What jobs were automated, how were they triggered, and how did you troubleshoot failed builds or test runs?
You have worked with Linux, UNIX, AIX, Solaris, and shell scripts. How would you investigate a production issue where a high-traffic web application is slow or unavailable on a Linux host?
What shell or batch scripts have you written, and can you walk through one that automated a testing, deployment, log-verification, or data-processing activity?
How have you used Jenkins, Maven, TestNG, and Selenium WebDriver together in an automated pipeline? How were test results and failures communicated to the team?
In the Spectrum ETL project, how did you validate data transformations across DI, DQ, or UAM modules? What checks did you perform at the source, transformation, and target layers?

This role requires monitoring, log analysis, and on-call support. Describe your experience verifying logs through UNIX or Linux. Which logs or error patterns did you look for, and how did you determine the likely cause of a failure?

How would you design a CI/CD workflow for a web application that needs controlled deployments across pre-production and production environments, including approval, rollback, and post-deployment validation?

The role uses AWS services such as EC2, S3, IAM, RDS, CloudWatch, Lambda, CloudFormation, and CDK. Based on your Linux, scripting, and Jenkins background, how would you approach learning and operating an AWS-hosted application platform?

Describe a defect you identified during integration or system testing that required coordination with developers or another team. How did you document it in Jira or Quality Center, validate the fix, and prevent regression?

Autodesk needs reliable, always-available platform services. What monitoring signals and alert thresholds would you define for a customer-facing web application and its database to support uptime and SLA objectives?
